title: Digital rain over a live HTML terminal
blurb: Cascading green phosphor code rain falls across a live HTML terminal on one WebGL 2 canvas, catching on typed letters, borders and buttons while keeping the input editable.
question: Can one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas cascade columns of glowing green phosphor digital code rain directly over a live interactive HTML terminal card, so HTML glyphs, borders and active buttons catch falling droplets and flare brighter green while the text underneath stays editable and clickable?
result: Measured in headless Chrome 160 Canary (2026-11-27): 6/6 live checks pass (927×1085 px, 1.01 MP at 412 px DPR 2.625, peak 2 WebGL contexts, 0 lost, 0 unasked readbacks). Typing and quick-command buttons re-upload #term-panel via texElementSubImage2D() while remaining hit-testable via updateElementGeometry(). Headless Chromium 157, npm run check:jank and real Chrome 159 on Android stay not verified.
